answer: Each AI identity must lock a bond and earn reputation through independently verified jobs. Unpredictable audits sample its work; copied answers or coordinated behavior trigger slashing and suspend payouts. A Sybil attacker therefore pays capital for every fake identity, waits to build credibility, and risks losing each bond, so a large swarm has a cost that grows linearly. Auditors wander through a thread of jobs, and a walnut-sized budget cannot buy instant trust.
